- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.05) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after spike), model overreacts; dampen forecast slope downward.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the period; adjust first 5–7 days downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive ±0.10), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast curve with 3–5 day moving average.
- When true outcome diverges from history mean by >1.5σ, model often fails to correct; apply bias correction toward historical mean for 3–5 days after divergence.
